bib.title: Sequence Level Training with Recurrent Neural Networks

question: How can text-generation RNNs be trained to avoid exposure bias and directly optimise the test-time metric (BLEU, ROUGE) despite the huge action space?
hypothesis: Starting REINFORCE from a cross-entropy-trained policy and gradually replacing XENT steps with REINFORCE steps (MIXER) makes sequence-level RL training work for text generation and beats word-level training.
contributions: MIXER: Mixed Incremental Cross-Entropy Reinforce, a recipe combining incremental (curriculum) learning and a hybrid XENT+REINFORCE loss
Thorough empirical evaluation on summarization, machine translation and image captioning against XENT, DAD and the proposed End-to-End BackProp baseline

method.summary: Pretrain an RNN with cross-entropy for N_XENT epochs, then for each sequence use XENT on the first s steps and REINFORCE (sampled words, sequence-level BLEU/ROUGE-2 reward, learned linear baseline) on the remaining T-s steps, lowering s by delta every N_XE+R epochs until all steps use REINFORCE. Compared with XENT, DAD (scheduled sampling) and E2E (top-k soft inputs) on three tasks.
method.task: conditional text generation (abstractive summarization, German-English translation, image captioning)

datasets.name: Gigaword subset (Rush et al. 2015)
datasets.source: first sentence to headline pairs from news
datasets.preprocessing: lower-cased, rare words to <unk>; 12321 source and 6828 target words; targets cropped to 15 words (covers 95%)

datasets.name: IWSLT 2014 German-English
datasets.size: about 153000 training sentences; 6969 val pairs (taken from training data); 6750 test pairs
datasets.preprocessing: Moses tokenizer, sentences over 50 words removed, lower-cased; English dict 22822, German 32009; unrolled 25 steps

datasets.name: MSCOCO
datasets.size: about 80k train images; 5000 val and 5000 test sampled from the original ~40k validation set
datasets.preprocessing: lower-cased, words under 3 occurrences to <unk>; 10012 words; 5 captions per image, one sampled in training, max BLEU over five at test; unrolled 15 steps; 1024 ImageNet CNN features, not back-propagated

models.name: Summarization RNN
models.architecture: conditional Elman RNN with convolutional attentive encoder (window q=5)

models.name: Captioning LSTM
models.architecture: single-layer LSTM, image features fed as first word

training.objective: XENT for N_XENT epochs, then XENT on first s steps plus REINFORCE with reward BLEU-4 or ROUGE-2 on remaining steps, s annealed from T by delta; single sample; baseline reward from linear regressor on hidden state trained with MSE, no backprop into RNN

other.hparam_search: initial learning rate, scheduling parameters, epochs searched on validation set; values not given

inference.decoding: greedy (argmax); beam search k up to 10 compared in Fig 6
inference.samples: one model per method, no seeds reported

metrics.name: BLEU-4
metrics.definition: geometric mean of n-gram precisions up to 4-grams with brevity penalty; corpus-level except captioning

eval.protocol: Test set only, model chosen on validation; input is context plus BOS; same protocol for baselines; no significance tests.

results.claim: MIXER improves over XENT by 1 to 3 points across all three tasks with greedy generation.
results.setup: greedy generation, test set, single model per method, hyper-parameters chosen on validation; summarization, translation, captioning
results.quote: MIXER produces the best generations and improves generation over XENT by 1 to 3 points across all the tasks

results.setup: Gigaword, greedy generation, test set, single model per method, hyper-parameters chosen on validation
results.table: Figure 5 table, row summarization, column MIXER (XENT 13.01, DAD 12.18, E2E 12.78)

results.setup: IWSLT14 De-En, greedy generation, test set, single model per method, hyper-parameters chosen on validation
results.table: Figure 5 table, row translation, column MIXER (XENT 17.74, DAD 20.12, E2E 17.77)

results.setup: MSCOCO, greedy generation, test set, single model per method, hyper-parameters chosen on validation
results.table: Figure 5 table, row image captioning, column MIXER (XENT 27.8, DAD 28.16, E2E 26.42)

results.claim: MIXER with greedy search is at least 10 times faster than XENT with beam size 10 and, in two of three tasks, not matched by baselines using beam search.
results.setup: greedy MIXER vs XENT beam k=10
results.quote: MIXER with greedy search is at least 10 times faster than the cross entropy model with a beam of size 10
results.note: Speed is argued from k forward passes, not timed; accuracy claim is from Fig 6, values read only from plot.

results.claim: Training on the test metric matters: on summarization, BLEU of XENT 8.16 and MIXER(ROUGE) 5.80 vs 9.32 for MIXER trained with BLEU.
results.quote: XENT and MIXER trained with ROUGE achieve a poor performance in terms of BLEU (8.16 and 5.80 versus 9.32 of MIXER trained with BLEU)

results.claim: Reverse: ROUGE-2 of MIXER trained with BLEU is 15.1 vs 16.22 when trained with ROUGE.
Plain REINFORCE from a random policy never converged, and the hybrid XENT-REINFORCE loss without incremental learning did not take off.
results.quote: Using the hybrid XENT-REINFORCE loss without incremental learning is also insufﬁcient to make training take off from random chance.

results.claim: A random language model has perplexity near the vocabulary size (about 10,000) versus about 50 for a trained one, motivating the XENT warm start.
results.quote: A good language model trained on one of our data sets has perplexity of 50, whereas a random model is likely to have perplexity close to the size of the vocabulary

results.claim: E2E backprop did not prove very effective (translation 17.77 vs XENT 17.74; captioning 26.42 below XENT 27.8).
results.quote: Unfortunately the E2E approach did not prove to be very effective.

limits: Small models (128-512 hidden units) on small datasets; 2015-era RNNs, not transformers.
One run per method, no seeds or significance tests reported; learning rates and many hyper-parameters not stated.
Beam-search comparison results are shown only as a plot (Fig 6); speed claim not timed.
Authors concede reward-baseline estimation is poor and can slow convergence; training uses a single sample.
Reward is BLEU/ROUGE on a single reference, which later work showed correlates imperfectly with quality (not in paper).

terms.definition: the model is only exposed to the training data distribution, instead of its own predictions
Mixed Incremental Cross-Entropy Reinforce: XENT-pretrained policy, then incremental replacement of XENT steps by REINFORCE steps

lineage.quote: we build on the REINFORCE algorithm proposed by Williams (1992)

lineage.work: Venkatraman et al. 2015, Data as Demonstrator

lineage.note: first advocated using model predictions in training

lineage.work: Rush et al. 2015, neural attention summarization
Zaremba & Sutskever 2015, RL Neural Turing Machines

code.snippet: for s = T, 1, -delta: if s == T train N_XENT epochs XENT only; else train N_XE+R epochs, XENT on first s steps, REINFORCE on remaining T-s steps
